properties.digitization_method: NEWLY ADDED 2026-09-16 -- user pointed out that the already-tracked 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' polygon (0.4 acres, near the pier's point/breakwater) should connect to Blocks 4 and 9 and to Humboldt Street Plaza, and should not overlap Block 9. That file's own regulatory_context already noted it covers only ~0.4 of a ~2-acre 'Prequel Park' interim open-space project (SF Port Commission Resolution 25-70, Nov 18 2025, amending Lease L-16662) -- the other ~1.6 acres sits on Potrero Power Station's own land (not Port jurisdiction), which had never been separately tracked. A construction-pipeline document (Spring 2026 dev forecast) independently describes this same project as a '2-acre Waterfront Park', strongly suggesting this Power-Station-land portion is the same physical shoreline corridor already traced (less precisely, and for a different purpose) as this dataset's separate 'Waterfront Park' feature (a D4D-diagram-labeled, long-term planning feature, sourced and georeferenced completely differently). Built this connector polygon by combining two already-validated sources rather than re-tracing from scratch: (1) the WEST/inner edge uses Block 4, Humboldt Street Plaza, and Block 9's own already-committed corners directly, so it shares an exact boundary with all three and cannot overlap Block 9 by construction; (2) the EAST/shoreline edge reuses Waterfront Park's own previously satellite-color-validated outer-shoreline trace (see that file's digitization_method for how it was built) between Block 4's latitude and Prequel Park (Port sub-area)'s own northernmost point, where the two pieces meet and touch -- except for a ~20m notch in that trace (its own vertices between the point at lon -122.38137/lat 37.75663 and the point at lon -122.38137/lat 37.75629) that pre-dated Block 9's GDAL/TPS correction and dipped into Block 9's real footprint; dropped those points since the west-edge chain now defines that boundary directly. STATUS CORRECTED 2026-09-24: this record's own dossier (data/records/prequel_park_power_station_subarea.json) had, since its creation, carried a summary and milestone history saying no source confirms construction has started, and its own open_questions explicitly flagged this file's 'under_construction' status as wrong ('Recommend planned until a dated source appears') -- that recommendation was never applied. A site visitor caught the resulting bug directly: the site showed 'under construction' today but reverted to 'planned' a couple of years into the future on the timeline scrubber, because the only real dated milestone with a status is the 2020-04-21 entitlement ('planned'), and the record's own future-projection milestone for 2026 is itself expected+'planned' (construction hasn't started yet, per every source), while the live status field alone (read only exactly at 'today') was stuck on the older, unsourced 'under_construction' value. Corrected to 'planned' to match the record's own sourced research and remove the contradiction; sibling record 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' already correctly says 'planned'. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: this file cited no source (source_doc_urls was empty); it now lists the Port Commission memo of Nov 14, 2025 (Calendar Item 10A), the final D4D and the SF Chronicle of May 22, 2025. (1) The Port Commission adopted Resolution 25-70 amending Lease L-16662 on Nov 18, 2025 (Port Commission minutes), and the memo (p.3) says the park covers approximately 2 acres with approximately 0.4 acre on the Port premises; the '~1.6 acres' on Power Station land in the log above is our own subtraction, not a sourced figure. (2) The log above says a Spring 2026 construction-pipeline document independently describes the project as a '2-acre Waterfront Park'; that document could not be located online or checked, so it should not be relied on. The '2-acre' size is supported by the Port memo instead. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, why_no_real_parcel, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- this polygon combines two different sourcing methods (see digitization_method) and has not been independently re-verified as a whole against satellite imagery. Its west edge is exact (shared vertices with Block 4/Humboldt Street Plaza/Block 9). Its east/shoreline edge inherits whatever accuracy Waterfront Park's own trace has -- treat it as a reasonable but not freshly-verified approximation of the real shoreline. This is the 'Power Station sub-area' complement to 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' -- together they approximate the full ~2-acre interim park project, though the true internal boundary between Port and Power-Station land has not been independently confirmed. The ~2-acre figure is stated in the Port Commission memo of Nov 14, 2025 (Calendar Item 10A, p.3: Prequel Park 'will cover approximately 2 acres, of which approximately .4 acres will be located on the Premises'); the press gives 2.5-2.75 acres.'; why_no_real_parcel: 'Open space with no subdivided Assessor parcel of its own within the largely unaddressed former power-station site. (This is our own parcel-search narration, not something any cited source establishes.)'; notes: 'Newly added 2026-09-16 to complement 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' -- see accuracy_caveat.'. CHECKED 2026-10-11: DataSF's active lot 4175028 (21,885 m2, 1241 Delaware St, PPS-MU zoning, recorded 2022-08-30) holds 3,743 m2 of this drawing. It also holds Blocks 3, 4 and 9, Humboldt Street Plaza and parts of Prequel Park and Waterfront Park, so the owner reads it as an undivided parent lot; this park has no lot of its own and the drawing is kept. properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- Pier & Point's own composition, not a drawn plan: no source read draws Prequel Park's boundary (the Port memo's Exhibit 1 is an unscaled schematic of the ownership sub-areas and the interim improvements; the Power Station website's map page shows an aerial rendering with no outline). The shape is the band of shoreline between Block 9's south edge and Block 4's north edge (each extended to the shore), joined with Block 9, Block 4 and Humboldt Street Plaza, which the interim park is read to occupy until those are built. That makes it 13,876 m2 (3.4 acres). Sources give about 2 acres (Port memo, Calendar Item 10A, Nov 14, 2025), 2.5 acres (Power Station website) and 2.75 acres (press), so none of these figures is certain. It overlaps Block 9, Block 4 and the plaza on purpose, and the overlap ends when those are built.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no Assessor lot of its own: 92% of the shape lies inside DataSF's active lot 4175028 (21,885 m2, 1241 Delaware St), an undivided lot that also holds Blocks 3, 4 and 9, Humboldt Street Plaza, the Stack and parts of the shoreline parks (checked 2026-10-11).
properties.regulatory_context: The Potrero Power Station-land portion of the ~2-acre Prequel Park interim open-space project (see 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' for the Port-jurisdiction portion and its own sourcing; the Port memo of Nov 14, 2025 puts about 0.4 acre on the Port premises). Per the Port memo the park is to include a multi-purpose lawn and sport courts, amphitheater seating, a quarter-mile walking and running track, water access and restrooms. Construction start is targeted for the third quarter of 2026 per the memo's p.4 (p.2 says the first quarter of 2026); no source confirms a start, so the status is 'planned'.
properties.notes: Added 2026-09-16 to complement 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' -- see the accuracy note for this shape. The shoreline strip of this park is read to be the ground the permanent Waterfront Park is built on when the interim park ends, and Blocks 4 and 9 and Humboldt Street Plaza are built over the rest. Since 2026-10-11 this record covers the whole interim Prequel Park (the Power Station and Port sub-areas together) and is shown over Blocks 4 and 9 and Humboldt Street Plaza until they are built.

properties.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outlines; not tied to an Assessor parcel), cross-confirmed against ESRI World Imagery satellite tiles. This replaced, on 2026-09-17, a long chain of diagram- and text-based approximations (their sources are kept below for history). How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record). Originally three converging real-world sources: (1) 2011 Port RFI "Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan" map (sfport.com/sites/default/files/FileCenter/Documents/939-Pier70_RFI_3-2-11_web.pdf, PDF p.11), a scaled map with real street labels (Illinois St, 20th St) showing Building 21 immediately adjacent to Building 12 near the historic core, annotated "BUILDING 21 PROPOSED TO BE RELOCATED"; (2) Aug 3 2017 Port Commission memo (sfport.com/sites/default/files/Commission/Item%2011A%20Pier%2070%20Final.pdf, Exhibit F p.68): "Building 21 (Substation No. 5)... would be relocated approximately 75 feet to the southeast, and in its new location it would front Slipways Commons... sits directly next to the proposed new waterfront arts facility" (future tense: a planned relocation as part of the rehabilitation); (3) D4D Figure 3.6.1 "Illustrative Slipways Commons Plan" (p.56/PDF p.72), a scaled plan with a real 0-50-100ft bar and "MARYLAND ST" label, captioned "the historic node of Buildings 2, 12, and 21."
properties.digitization_method: REFIT 2026-09-13 with src/block_fit.py, on top of two prior corrections. (1) THIS PROJECT'S OWN real Building 12 anchor was wrong: status.csv had Building 12 joined to blklot 4045017 (700 Illinois St), an unrelated residential condo building over 500m from the real Building 12 -- corrected to 1070 Maryland St, blklot 4114010; see status.csv. (2) After correcting the anchor, this polygon (and Elevation Sky Park) was placed as a hand-computed offset rectangle, and a user screenshot showed it still crossing a real street -- the hand-computed street setbacks were not reliable. Replaced with a repeatable tool instead of a third hand computation: src/fetch_streets.py fetches real OSM street centerlines for the whole project area once (cached to data/raw/streets.geojson), and src/block_fit.py polygonizes them (plus the Port jurisdiction boundary, for shoreline-bounded blocks) into real block polygons, then fits a box of the requested size inside the correct one -- checked programmatically against every nearby street, not eyeballed. This building's real block (Maryland/21st/22nd St, the same one Elevation Sky Park occupies) is a real, well-formed small block, so block_fit.py fit it at its full documented 101ft x 75ft size, no shrinking needed, in the southern part of that block (nearer Building 12/22nd St); Elevation Sky Park occupies the rest of the same block to its north/east. ROTATED 2026-09-13: block_fit.py's earlier version always produced a true-north-aligned box, which looked visibly wrong once rendered -- this area's real street grid (Maryland/Louisiana/Delaware St etc.) is rotated relative to true north, and an axis-aligned box in a rotated block wastes space and doesn't match its neighbors' orientation. fit_box now rotates the box to match the bearing of the nearest real street segment before fitting/shrinking it. OVERLAP NOTE 2026-09-14 (project-wide overlap audit, SUPERSEDED 2026-09-16, see below): Fully overlapped Pier 70 Parcel E2 at the time -- expected given this marker's own low-confidence, directional-only placement; not clipped, since doing so would erase the marker entirely rather than usefully correct it. RE-TRACED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 deep pass, after applying Potrero's GCP-validation lessons to Pier 70's own transform): rather than continue relying on block_fit.py's street-polygon-fit approach (which only guarantees this box sits somewhere inside the right real block, not at a source-verified position), went back to the same source diagram used for this site's numbered parcels -- Figure 6.4.2 (Building Height Maximum), which shows Building 21 directly as one of its labeled gray 'Historic Buildings' boxes -- and pixel-traced its box directly (programmatic pixel-color sampling to find the box's true edges, at x=1551-1651, y=833-909 in the 2376x1836px source image, after an initial visual estimate proved off by ~55-60px on a badly-scaled crop). Converted via this site's validated 6-point affine transform (the same one used for Parcels A-H, residual error 1-8m against 5 real street intersections plus Building 12's real Assessor centroid) -- NOT block_fit.py's separate street-polygonize method. Cross-checked the transform itself against Building 12's real centroid (blklot 4114010) before trusting this result, per the lesson learned from Potrero's mis-measured-GCP incident: the transform reproduces Building 12's real-world position acceptably well, so it is not grossly miscalibrated. RESULT (2026-09-16, later superseded -- see below): this diagram-derived position was initially found to overlap Pier 70 Parcel E1 by 429.8 m2. FALSE ALARM, RESOLVED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass, later same day): a user-flagged visual check found E1's own traced shape was badly wrong (a misshapen quadrilateral that cut through this very '21' box and the open space beyond it, rather than the real L-shaped 90ft/65ft footprint shown on Figure 6.4.2). E1 was re-traced programmatically from its own two legend colors -- see pier70_e1.geojson's digitization_method -- and the overlap with this file dropped to exactly 0 m2, confirming Building 21's own position here was correct all along; the earlier overlap was entirely an artifact of E1's bad shape. Still overlapped 'Elevation Sky Park' by 275 m2 (unaffected by the E1 fix) -- see accuracy_caveat. RESOLVED 2026-09-17: that separate ESP entry was merged into Pier 70 Parcel E3's own row per an explicit user decision (see pier70_e3.geojson) and is no longer plotted as its own block, so this overlap no longer applies -- kept here for history. UPGRADED TO REAL FOOTPRINT 2026-09-17 (user request: 'building 21 can be more precise by leveraging satellite image, since it's an existing building that will remain'): rather than keep tracing/re-fitting a hand-drawn box, searched DataSF's Building Footprints dataset for real structures near this site (mblr=SF4052001 -- the same giant, largely-unsubdivided Assessor lot found to underlie much of central Pier 70, also covering Building 14; see status.csv's 4052001 row) and rendered all of them directly over ESRI World Imagery satellite tiles. That rendering showed two real, adjacent dark-roofed structures (367.8 and 367.2 sq m, combined 734.96 sq m / ~7,911 sqft) sitting almost exactly under this file's own previously-committed diagram-derived box -- a close match (within 4.4%) to the previously-cited 101ft x 75ft (~703.7 sq m) footprint size. A third, larger nearby footprint (1,879.7 sq m) that a pure diagram-position guess had initially favored turned out, on the satellite image, to actually be a paved section of Maryland St itself (a street mistakenly captured as a 'building' in the source dataset) -- not a structure at all; ruled out once seen against real imagery, exactly the kind of error satellite cross-checking is meant to catch. A small adjacent 49 sq m footprint sits ~9m south of the two main pieces (not touching) -- possibly a small appendage or a separate utility structure; not confirmed, so not included. Replaced the hand-traced diagram box with the union of the two matched real footprints (MultiPolygon, since DataSF's extraction has them as two separate touching-but-unmerged pieces). Checked for overlap against E1, E3, E4, Parcel D, Building 2, and Building 12's real parcel -- zero overlap with all of them at this corrected, smaller, more precisely-positioned footprint. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: (a) The Assessor parcels named above for Building 12 (blklot 4114010, 1070 Maryland St) and for the wrong earlier join (blklot 4045017, listed by DataSF at 700 Illinois St) come from DataSF's Assessor parcels (repo copy data/raw/parcels.geojson) and status.csv, not from the URLs cited in this file; the earlier description of 4045017 as an 'unrelated residential condo building' more than 500 m away is our own observation, not a sourced fact. (b) The footprint areas (367.8 and 367.2 sq m; a 1,879.7 sq m 'building' that is paved Maryland St) and the legacy lot id mblr SF4052001 are from DataSF Building Footprints (repo copy data/raw/buildings.geojson), a dataset not listed in source_doc_urls; the satellite reading is our own judgement. properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-17. China Basin Park (the Design Controls' name; 'Mission Rock Park' in the 2012 proposal) opened April 2024 with Phase 1 (sfyimby.com, 2024-04-26). Its real Assessor lot is 8719A005: 18,975 m2 / 4.69 ac, created when Seawall Lot 337 was subdivided in 2020. The lot has not been split, so this feature is the recorded lot geometry (223 vertices, simplified to 2e-7 deg / ~2 cm) minus that lobe, cut exactly along the lobe's recorded north line so the park and Block K touch with no gap; a 99 m2 sliver left along the paseo lot line by the cut was dropped. Area 186,359 sf (4.28 ac) vs 204,246 sf for the whole lot; the Design Controls and Phase 1 submittal describe the park as ~5 acres, the 2012 parcel table as 5.12 ac including Block K's frontage. OpenStreetMap's park polygon (way 27656676, 19,480 m2) has IoU 0.76 with the whole lot and also includes the K lobe; the recorded lot is used as the higher-authority boundary, per the definition of done. Routed through approximate_projects.csv rather than status.csv (like Crane Cove Park and the Pier 70 building footprints) only because the K lobe had to be carved out; if the Assessor splits Block K off, replace this file with a status.csv row on the park's new lot. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: (a) the lobe measures 139 x 143 ft in this file's own trace; the Design Controls' Appendix p.198 gives Block K as 139 ft x 144 ft (illustrative), so 'exactly Block K's site' overstates the match (within about 1 ft). properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-17 (site-completeness pass against Design Controls Figure 3.1.1). Channel Wharf is the paved waterfront plaza between Piers 48 and 50, east of Terry A Francois Boulevard, at the end of the Channel Street / Square / Channel Lane axis. The 2020 subdivision gave the TAFB right-of-way lot 8719A003 a rectangular notch there -- north edge shared with the Pier 48 lot 8719A001, east edge 27 m out at the wharf face, south edge on Pier 50's north line -- so the polygon is that notch, using the lots' own four recorded vertices (21,142 sf, 0.49 ac). Cross-check: IoU 0.65 against the green Channel Wharf fill traced independently on Figure 1.1 through its own transform (RMS 1.1 m); the figure's fill runs a few metres further east over the water edge than the lot line does, and its west edge is drawn at the TAFB shared zone rather than the lot line, which explains the difference. Not registered in verify_block_fill.py (no fill on Figure 6.2).
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE but high confidence: all four edges are recorded DataSF lot lines (the notch of lot 8719A003), agreeing with the Design Controls figures to within a few metres. Planned open space. The Design Controls (April 24, 2018, Section 3.5) describe Channel Wharf as continuing 'to serve as a functioning wharf while providing public access'; what occupies the notch today has not been checked against a current source.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: The wharf is part of the Terry A Francois Boulevard right-of-way lot 8719A003 (DataSF Assessor parcels, recorded 2020-06-12), which also carries the roadway and its paseo; joining status.csv to that lot would paint the whole boulevard (our mapping rationale, not a statement of the Design Controls).

The polygon uses that lot's recorded vertices for its west (Block K / park-lot lobe), north (park lot) and east (Pier 48 lot) edges, and closes on the south by extending the north lot line of the Exposition Street lot 8719A010 east to the Pier 48 lot line. Satellite imagery shows it as the paved road to the Pier 48 gate today. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: (a) The statement above that the first two paseos 'were built with Phase 1' rests on the Port Commission's Feb 11, 2025 minutes (https://sfport.com/media/10214/download), which record staff's request to accept Phase 1's public infrastructure and describe 'the paseos in the bottom around Building G leading in to China Basin Park' as Port owned (Resolutions 25-05, 25-06), and on the Port's June 5, 2026 report (Phase 1 completed in 2025; 'The City has accepted all Phase 1 public infrastructure'); neither names lots 8719B001 or 8719A007. The two lots are active DataSF Assessor parcels recorded 2020-06-12 (acdm-wktn). The Design Controls, this file's only earlier source_doc_url, say none of this. (b) The sentence 'Satellite imagery shows it as the paved road to the Pier 48 gate today' had no imagery source cited and was not re-checked; treat it as an unverified observation. (c) Vertex check against DataSF's lot vertices: three of the four vertices sit within 0.1 m of recorded lot corners; the south-east vertex, on the extended Exposition Street line, is about 23 m from the nearest recorded lot vertex. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, why_no_real_parcel reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE but high confidence on three edges (recorded lot lines); the south edge is the Exposition Street lot line extended ~23 m east, which is where the plan's Exposition Street right-of-way ends at TAFB. Planned (Design Controls Section 4.3.4: the boulevard 'will become a paseo'); no source read describes its current use. ANGLE CHECK: check_geometry_quality.py flags a 12.3-12.6 deg corner here (its tolerance is 12 deg). Three of this polygon's four vertices are real, recorded DataSF Assessor lot corners; the south-east vertex is not, since it closes the south edge on the extended Exposition Street line (see digitization_method). The flagged deviation is at two of the recorded corners, so it is the real lots' own shape (Bridgeview Way's paseo lot 8719A007 and the Exposition Street lot 8719A010 meet the park lot 8719A005 at a corner that is not exactly square), not a shear or a misread trace. Phase 1's delivery of the paseos is supported (Port Commission minutes, Feb 11, 2025; Port memo of June 5, 2026: 'The City has accepted all Phase 1 public infrastructure'), but no source read names those lots. DataSF lists 8719A007 at 1044-1046 Bridgeview Way (a Bridgeview Way address, consistent with the Bridgeview Street paseo) and 8719B001 with no address; 8719B001 lies between lots 8719B002 and 8719A008 by centroid, consistent with the Shared Public Way. (b) The closing south line is taken from the north line of the Exposition Street lot 8719A010, which in DataSF Parcels (acdm-wktn, data_as_of 2026-10-01, read 2026-10-12) carries date_rec_drop 2025-03-18 and project_id_drop 2025P8719 while active is still true (no reason given), so that line is the Assessor-data line, not a confirmed current legal boundary. (c) The sentence 'Satellite imagery shows it as the paved road to the Pier 48 gate today' still cites no image source and was not re-verified; entry (b) of the 2026-09-29 audit stands and it should be read as unconfirmed. No geometry was changed.

properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. RE-TRACED 2026-09-16 (full Pier 70 geometry restart, after a systematic pass found 9 of this site's other 'trusted' parcels were meaningfully wrong): re-measured programmatically instead of by eye, for consistency with the rest of this site -- isolated this legend color (RGB [128,193,219]) and extracted a clean rectangular contour (OpenCV) at pixel (1203,437)-(1401,682). Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. Result is close to (within ~5m of) the prior hand-read version -- this parcel's own corners were already read correctly; kept for methodological consistency across the site. Still overlaps 'Noonan Building' by ~2843 m2 -- an already-documented, expected overlap given Noonan's own low-confidence, directional-only placement. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the 'Building 14 footprint' identified by blklot 4052001 refers to a legacy lot id: DataSF Building Footprints carry mblr SF4052001 on 21 footprints in the repo copy (data/raw/buildings.geojson), the data do not show which is Building 14, and blklot 4052001 was retired on 2018-10-02 (DataSF Assessor parcels, acdm-wktn), so it is not a current Assessor lot. No outside source is cited for that identification. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (Port Item 11A, Aug 2026: the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'), and no source read ties it to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor parcels include new lots created for the 28-acre district in 2019, without street addresses, but which lot (if any) is Parcel A's was not established. It currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. EXTENDED SOUTH 2026-09-17 (user-flagged): this block's south edge fell ~11m short of the real sidewalk visible in satellite imagery, leaving a strip of unclaimed vacant land between the block and the street -- consistent with this site's known local scale error for parcels far from the transform's Illinois/Michigan St anchors (see Parcel E1's digitization_method for the same root cause). The diagram itself (Figure 6.4.2) shows this block's fill running right up to the street with no setback, so extended the two south vertices by 11m (measured via satellite pixel-color transition to the real sidewalk, 3 sample transects) to close the gap, matching the diagram's own convention rather than re-deriving the whole transform.'; notes: 'Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat.'. REPLACED 2026-10-10 (shape; status and use unchanged): the owner asked for the planned blocks that have Assessor lots under them to use those lots. DataSF's Assessor layer (data/raw/parcels.geojson) has Assessor lot 4111009 (5,013 m2, active, recorded 2019-02-07), 76% of our earlier trace lies inside it and the trace covers 81% of it; against the satellite imagery the lot lines sit on the real block edges where the trace was a few metres off. The outline is now that lot using the lots' own vertices (no simplification), in place of the traced shape of 5,307 m2. This identification is an inference from location, shape and size; no Port document read names the lot. geometry_type is now 'real' because the edges are recorded lot lines. The earlier sign-off covered the traced shape; this replacement was made at the owner's direction. 2026-10-12 CORRECTION to the 2026-10-10 entry above (text only; the shape is unchanged): its sentence 'against the satellite imagery the lot lines sit on the real block edges where the trace was a few metres off' was repeated across several Pier 70 shapes and no satellite comparison of this shape's edges is recorded, so the sentence is withdrawn for it. The lot is 5,013 m2 against a trace of 5,307 m2; 76% of the trace lies inside the lot and the trace covers 81% of it. No source read says so. Port Item 11A (Aug 7, 2026, p.2, Strategic Plan Objectives) says only 'Transform underutilized surface parking lots and warehouses into an equitable, accessible, and economically successful new mixed-use neighborhood' for the whole site and does not describe Parcel A's present condition, so the sentence is withdrawn and the note now says no source read describes what is on the block. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (twelfth pass): user confirmed the east edge and angled NE corner were correctly aligned to the real road/fence, but the other three edges were not -- rebuilt the whole polygon from those two confirmed-correct points (NE_cut, SE), deriving the site's real bearing directly from the confirmed east edge itself (not from Building 14 or an independent visual read) and constructing the west, top, and bottom edges as exactly parallel/perpendicular to it, using the previously-measured edge lengths for scale only. properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (second pass, same day): after the shear fix above, a user-flagged visual check still showed this block overlapping paved streets. Root cause found: several blocks (PKN, PKS, HDY3, HDY1/2, E4) had their OWN corner pixel positions misread during transcription -- e.g. PKN's west edge was recorded as pixel x=163 when the diagram's own gridline labels put it at x=355 (which is where the Illinois St anchor point itself was measured). This was a transcription slip, not a transform error -- the 6-point transform's anchors were unaffected (confirmed: A, B, C1, C2, D, E1, E2, E3, F/G, H1, H2 were read correctly the first time). Re-read all 5 affected blocks' corners directly against their crop images' own labeled gridlines and recomputed. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (fifth pass): user-flagged check found this block's boundary itself (not a clipping artifact) was missing an entire row of real, currently-used parking near 20th St -- the diagram-derived north edge sat ~25m south of the lot's actual northern extent. Measured directly against satellite imagery (same method as the west-edge fixes on B/E1/E2) and moved the north edge to the real curb/crosswalk line at 20th St. CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-09-14 (seventh pass): user clarified the diagonal row of angled cars along this block's west side is curbside parking on Illinois Street itself, not part of the PKN/PKS parcel -- the earlier fixes had mistakenly extended the west edge to include it. Pulled the west edge back east to -122.3874, matching where the diagonal on-street parking row ends and the lot's own perpendicular-grid parking begins (visually distinct in the satellite image). CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (eighth pass): auditing this block for the same curb-vs-lot-line mistake found and fixed on Pier 70 Building 2 (see that file's digitization_method, failure mode 6 in src/bearing_trace.py), a user-flagged review found the north edge (set in the fifth pass above) still had exactly that bug -- it was anchored on the 20th St curb/crosswalk line, one row of real angled parking too far north. That front row runs at a different angle than the rest of the lot's parking, has no visible separation from the street/crosswalk itself (i.e. it reads as curbside street parking, not a lot with its own frontage), and is set off from the second (and subsequent) rows by a real gap with a visible pavement-color change -- the same 'significant white separation' signal already used to exclude curbside parking on this block's west edge. Re-anchored the north edge at that second-row transition (approx. lon -122.38695, lat 37.76041) using this site's established grid bearing and line_intersection(). This moved the north edge roughly 7-8m south of the fifth-pass version. THIS WAS WRONG, CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (ninth pass): user clarified the eighth pass misread the imagery -- the diagonal row immediately south of the street IS part of PKN's own lot (it shares the same angle and spacing as the rest of the lot's parking), not curbside street parking. What actually sits between the street and that row is a much thinner sliver -- a single line of vehicles parked facing a DIFFERENT direction (parallel to the curb, not angled into the lot) -- that thin sliver, not the whole first diagonal row, is the real on-street parking to exclude, and it has no visible delimitation from the street itself (matching the earlier west-edge lesson: on-street parking reads as part of the street, not the lot). Re-measured the true boundary at the top edge of the diagonal row (where the angled spaces actually begin, immediately past that thin curbside sliver and the street's own paved width): lon -122.38696, lat 37.76061 -- essentially the SAME position as the fifth-pass version (within ~1m), confirming the fifth pass had already found the right line and the eighth pass's 'fix' was a real regression, not a correction. Lesson generalized in src/bearing_trace.py: when applying the curbside-parking-exclusion pattern, check the EXCLUDED band's own vehicle orientation and depth before assuming a whole matching row is street parking -- a thin, differently-angled sliver right at the curb is the real signal, not simply 'the row closest to the street.' STILL WRONG, CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (tenth pass): the ninth-pass fix anchored the whole north edge on a SINGLE measured point (at the west end) plus the site's established perpendicular bearing (86.5 degrees), rather than this specific edge's own two-point bearing -- exactly the shortcut this project's own bearing_trace.py methodology warns against (derive an edge's bearing from that edge's own two endpoints, not a borrowed one), and it produced a line that hugged the real row's top edge correctly at the west end but drifted north into the gap above the row by the east end. User annotated two separate crops (west portion and east end near the building corner) showing the true row-top edge; extracted the marked line's actual pixel path in both images and converted to real coordinates (rather than eyeballing), giving two well-separated points -- (-122.38702427, 37.76055681) and (-122.38675117, 37.76056792) -- 24m apart. Their own bearing (87.06 degrees) is close to the established 86.5 (confirms the site bearing was never the problem) but using these two real points directly, rather than one point plus an assumed bearing, fixed the drift: the resulting edge now hugs the row's top consistently at both ends, confirmed by zooming into each end separately after the fix. STILL WRONG, CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (eleventh pass): user pointed out the tenth-pass line still cut through a visible sidewalk -- a clearly lighter, more uniform-toned paved band sitting between the excluded curbside sliver and the real diagonal parking, distinct in color/texture from the lot's own darker, worn pavement. Confirmed quantitatively: averaging pixel brightness in bands parallel to the tenth-pass line (canceling out individual-car noise) showed a bright, ~3.5m-deep band immediately south of that line before brightness dropped off into the lot's own darker pavement -- i.e. the tenth-pass line sat inside the sidewalk, not at its far edge. Moved the edge 3.65m further south (same bearing, both endpoints shifted equally) to the point where the bright band ends and the lot's own pavement begins. Overlay-confirmed at both ends: a clearly lighter band is now visible between the old and new lines, and the new line sits right at the top of the real parking row with no sidewalk-toned pavement above it. TWELFTH PASS, same day (west/east edges): user asked to apply the same color-based criteria to the west and east edges, which had not been re-audited since their much earlier fixes. West edge: found the committed line ran straight through a second, distinct column of diagonal parking, splitting it in half -- there is a real walkway/gap west of that column (between it and the truly-curbside first column along Illinois St), and the whole second column sits on the PKN side of that walkway. Moved the west edge (both NW and SW, same bearing, parallel shift) 5.27m further west to that walkway, confirmed by zooming into both a wide view and a close-up: the previously-split column is now fully included and the true curbside-only column stays excluded. East edge: initially over-corrected by expanding 5.5m east, based on a large open paved apron that had similar color/texture to the lot -- user caught this: a curving driveway edge visible at the south end of that same apron indicates it's a road/driveway curve, not more lot, despite the matching pavement color. Reverted the east edge (NE, SE) back to its prior, un-expanded position -- ground color alone was not sufficient here without also reading the shape of the boundary (a curving edge is a strong road/driveway signal that overrides a same-color match). REVERTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 border-alignment audit): the twelve satellite-imagery-driven passes above were built on a mistaken premise -- this project maps the D4D's PLANNED layout (including streets and open space not yet built) against today's satellite imagery as a backdrop, not the other way around. Snapping this parcel's boundary to today's real parking-lot striping was wrong: it silently deleted 'Public Open Space' shown directly on Figure 6.4.2 (a green strip between this block and 20th St) and erased '21ST ST (NEW)' entirely, a real, deliberately-labeled future street the diagram draws with its own paved width between PKN and PKS. Re-traced this block directly from Figure 6.4.2 instead: programmatic pixel-color detection (isolating this legend color, RGB [169,143,173]) found this block's own purple fill spans pixel x 420-665, y 475-787 in the 2376x1836 source image (y=475 is where the fill begins, south of the green open-space strip; y=787 is this block's south edge, north of 21ST ST (NEW)'s own ~35px/~20m-wide drawn width) -- converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform used for this site's other numbered parcels. This restores the diagram's own street and open-space gaps that the satellite-snapping passes had collapsed to zero. The satellite-based lessons above (curbside-parking exclusion, sidewalk-color detection, driveway-curve reading) remain useful technique notes for tracing REAL/existing features elsewhere in this project, but do not apply to this PLANNED parcel's own boundary. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (streets/block-alignment review, prompted by a user request to audit street alignment sitewide): the pixel measurement immediately above ('x 420-665, y 475-787') was taken from a 2376x1836-resolution copy of Figure 6.4.2, but was then run through this site's 6-point affine transform, which was calibrated against the 2200x1700-resolution page171.png -- a resolution mismatch that silently shifted this whole block by the 2376/2200 = 1.08x scale factor (the same class of bug independently found and fixed on Building 21's old trace). Re-measured directly on page171.png (2200x1700) with the same color-isolation method: this block's true purple fill is pixel (389,440)-(578,728), a clean rectangle -- notably narrower on the east side than the old (665, unscaled) reading, which turns out to have also simply misread that edge (verified: a pixel scan at y=600 shows the fill ending at x~578-580, then a black border, then white street pavement -- there is no fill out to x=615 (665/1.08), so the east edge was doubly wrong, not just unscaled). Cross-checked against the neighboring blocks this touches: the corrected PKN-PKS gap (21st St NEW) is now 15.4m (previously reported as 19-26m under the old, larger trace -- both are plausible street widths, but 15.4m is what the corrected geometry actually gives), and this fix also required correcting the '20th Street Plaza' frontage strip (data/manual/pier70_pkn_frontage_plaza.geojson), which had explicitly copied this block's old (wrong) x-range and south-edge y-value -- see that file's own digitization_method. CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-09-17 (same day, after PKS was found badly mispositioned): PKS was ground-truthed against the real 21st St centerline and moved ~25m south (see pier70_pks.geojson) -- as a direct consequence, this block's own south edge, while not itself overlapping any real street (only 4.5% buffer overlap, not flagged), left an oversized ~40m gap to PKS's new position, far wider than Figure 6.4.2's own drawn '21ST ST (NEW)' width (~20m) or this street's real curb-to-curb width (~13-15m, measured elsewhere in this project). Extended this block's own south edge further south to close that gap: interpolated the real 21st St centerline's latitude at this edge's own two longitudes and set the edge 6.8m north of it (the same real curb-to-centerline half-width used sitewide). New PKN-PKS gap is 13.5m, consistent with the street's real measured width; confirmed 0 overlap with 21st St itself. RE-INVESTIGATED 2026-09-17 (yet again, same day, after user feedback called the prior revert-and-redo cycle 'mostly a downgrade' and asked for a clarifying question rather than another guess): went back to first principles instead of more pixel geometry. Two checks, both requested by the user: (1) searched the D4D's own text (Section 4.11, Specific Streets Design Intent) for any description of 21st St being relocated or realigned -- found none; it describes 21st St as 'primarily serves as an alley from Illinois Street to the waterfront,' with no mention of a moved alignment. (2) Pulled real satellite imagery (src/satellite_check.py) directly over where DataSF's official centerline (CNN 15232000/15233000) says 21st St runs between Illinois and Michigan St -- it shows vegetation, graded dirt, a tree, and a vehicle-storage yard: zero pavement. So the earlier 'the D4D relocates 21st St' theory (this file's own prior REVERTED/RETRACTED entries) was an overreach from a real but simpler fact: DataSF's centerline here is a paper (platted, unbuilt) alignment, the same failure mode as three other already-excluded CNNs in street_geometry.py (12915000, 15200000, 15228000) -- not a deliberate relocation. Added CNN 15232000/15233000 to that same exclusion list, with the satellite evidence documented there. User's explicit instruction: note that this stretch of 21st St isn't built yet, but for this map's purpose (showing the planned FUTURE parcel state) treat the diagram's own drawn '21ST ST (NEW)' position as authoritative. Restored this block to its pure diagram-transform position accordingly -- the same value already found and confirmed multiple times this project (most recently before the mistaken ground-truth shift below). REPOSITIONED 2026-09-17 (user override: 'take my input as override... turn that Michigan span into 21st st and adjust parcel positioning accordingly'): re-anchored to the corrected planned 21st St line (see pier70_21st_street.geojson -- built from Michigan St's own real terminus point, perpendicular to Illinois/Louisiana's real ~175.5-degree bearing), replacing the Figure 6.4.2 pixel-traced position used previously. Only this block's south edge changes (north/east/west edges, anchored to real 20th St, are untouched): snapped to the new anchor line's position 6.8m north of its centerline (this project's curb half-width) at each corner's own longitude. This block grows -- its south edge moves further south than the previous pixel-traced position, since the new, real-anchored '21st St (NEW)' sits further south than the diagram pixel trace did. ADJUSTED 2026-09-17 (two user-flagged issues, same pass): (1) east edge extended to real Michigan St (this block's previous east edge stopped well short of Michigan St's real position, leaving an unclaimed ~13-19m gap the user called out as 'arbitrary') -- computed Michigan's real centerline (CNN 8999001) at this block's own corner latitudes and set the edge 9.8m west of it (6.8m curb + ~3m sidewalk allowance, per the D4D's own cited 55-67ft ROW range for this class of street). (2) north edge moved south by 10m ('a notch,' a judgment call per the user's own phrasing, not a diagram or survey measurement) to give the 20th St Plaza more depth, since this block's own south edge had already grown substantially in the prior round -- see pier70_pkn_frontage_plaza.geojson for the matching extension. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: 'HDY3 should border Illinois like PKS and PKN, in the continuity'): this block's own SW corner, PKS's NW/SW corners, and HDY3's NW corner had each been independently traced/measured against Illinois St at different times, leaving a several-meter 'wobble' between the three blocks' own west edges instead of one continuous line. Recomputed this block's SW corner from a single shared formula (used identically on PKS and HDY3): interpolate real Illinois St's centerline (CNN 7169000) longitude at this corner's own latitude, then offset 9.8m east (this project's standard curb+sidewalk allowance) -- see pier70_hdy3.geojson's own digitization_method for the full writeup covering all three blocks together. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the Assessor identifiers named in this log (Building 14's footprint as blklot 4052001; Building 12's Assessor parcel as blklot 4114010) come from DataSF (Building Footprints and Assessor parcels; repo copies in data/raw), not from the D4D cited for this file. Blklot 4052001 is a legacy lot: DataSF retired it on 2018-10-02 (Assessor parcels, acdm-wktn), its footprints carry mblr SF4052001, and the footprint layer does not name any of them 'Building 14'. Blklot 4114010 is an active lot at 1070 Maryland St that DataSF does not name 'Building 12'; that identity rests on the address given in tenant sources. Also, the Michigan St offset of 9.8 m described above as 'per the D4D's own cited 55-67ft ROW range for this class of street' cites the wrong class: D4D S4.2.1 gives the 55-67 ft ROW range to 20th, 22nd and Maryland Streets, while Michigan Street is in the class limited to 30-55 ft; the 9.8 m offset (6.8 m curb plus a ~3 m sidewalk allowance) is our own estimate, not a D4D figure. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (the developers' pages call it 'fully entitled' and Handel Architects lists it 'In Design'; no groundbreaking was found in any source read), and no source read identifies its Assessor lot: it was sold by the Port outright (Presidio Bay's page calls it 'the only privately-owned land in the Pier 70 Special Use District'), and DataSF's Assessor parcels list active P70-MU lots at about this location (for example lot 4110012 at 919 Illinois St, and lot 4110009 with no address), but which of them is Parcel K North's was not established. It currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district. RE-TRACED 2026-09-17 directly from Figure 6.4.2 at the correct source resolution (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. This deliberately does NOT match today's satellite imagery of the parking lot -- this parcel's boundary represents the D4D's planned footprint, including '21ST ST (NEW)' and the '20th Street Plaza' open-space strip (data/manual/pier70_pkn_frontage_plaza.geojson), neither of which is built yet.'; notes: 'Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat. properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass): Figure 3.3.1 shows a landscaped strip along Parcel K North (PKN)'s own 20th Street frontage -- a hardscape/lawn/seating area distinct from PKN's own building footprint -- that was not yet tracked in this dataset at all (this dataset had zero Pier 70 open-space features before this pass, unlike Potrero which has four). Confirmed Figure 3.3.1 shares the exact same page layout/pixel grid as Figure 6.4.2 (verified by overlaying already-traced parcel boundaries from 6.4.2 directly onto 3.3.1 -- they align pixel-for-pixel), so this site's already-validated 6-point affine transform (see Pier 70 Parcel A's digitization_method) was reused directly rather than re-deriving a new one. Traced this strip's bounding box directly: pixel x 420-665 (matching PKN's own east-west extent exactly, so this shares an exact boundary with PKN and cannot overlap it), y 401-475 (from the site's own Project Site Boundary line at 20th St down to where PKN's own building fill begins). This is a simplified bounding-box trace of an illustrative (non-dimensioned) rendering -- Figure 3.3.1 shows internal detail (a gated courtyard-like area, lawn panels, and a seating/game-court area) that this polygon does not attempt to subdivide. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (streets/block-alignment review): both pixel values above ('x 420-665', 'y...475') were inherited directly from PKN's own 2376x1836-resolution measurement, which turned out to have been run through the 2200x1700-calibrated affine transform unrescaled -- a confirmed bug (see pier70_pkn.geojson's digitization_method) that also mismeasured PKN's east edge independent of the scale error. Since this plaza was defined to share PKN's exact x-range by construction, it inherited both problems. Corrected to match PKN's newly-retraced, correct-resolution contour exactly: x 389-578 (PKN's real east-west extent), y 371-440 (440 = PKN's corrected north edge, matched exactly so the shared boundary still can't overlap; 371 = 401/1.08, rescaling the south-boundary-line pixel reading since it comes from Figure 3.3.1, not 6.4.2, and there is no independent legend-color fill to re-detect there). Confirmed 0m gap / 0 overlap against the corrected PKN. EXEMPTED FROM STREET CLIPPING 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: 'tiny and divided by the road'): join_approximate.py's automatic real-street clip was silently discarding ~69% of this feature (leaving a ~384 sq m sliver of the traced ~1,255 sq m, and splitting it into disconnected fragments where the real street's buffer cut through it) -- which is exactly what 'tiny and divided by the road' looks like. Investigated whether this was the same kind of mispositioning bug found on C1/PKS: it is not. This strip's whole purpose (per Figure 3.3.1) is to replace part of TODAY's wider real 20th Street with tomorrow's narrower street + landscaped frontage -- the same 'the diagram's plan overrides today's satellite imagery' principle already hard-won on PKN itself (see that file's own extensive revert history, where satellite-snapping this exact frontage was tried and explicitly reverted for the same reason). Real curb data here doesn't cleanly separate 'street' from 'lot' anyway (this whole area is currently one undifferentiated surface parking lot, same ambiguity documented on PKS before its own unrelated positioning bug was found). Set street_clip_exempt so this feature renders at its full traced size against the real, planned frontage depth Figure 3.3.1 shows, rather than being cut down to whatever survives clipping against a street this plan is meant to narrow. REVERSED 2026-09-17, SAME DAY (user-flagged: 'not on 20th street? Should be south of 20th'): wrong call -- checked where this polygon's north edge actually sits relative to the real 20th St centerline (not just the buffer) and found it extends 70-95m PAST the centerline, onto the north side of 20th Street entirely (into the block containing Buildings 102/104), not just a modest planned narrowing of the near curb. The 'illustrative rendering, rescaled pixel estimate' north edge (see above) was simply wrong, not a legitimate planned encroachment -- removed street_clip_exempt and properly ground-truthed this edge instead: interpolated the real 20th St centerline's latitude at this polygon's own two longitudes and set the north edge 6.8m south of it (this project's standard real curb-to-centerline half-width). Available real depth here is thin (4-6m, similar to PKN's own south-edge finding against 21st St) -- resulting area is ~305 sq m, much smaller than the original ~1,255 sq m illustrative-bbox trace. This is a real, if narrow, sidewalk-scale frontage strip, not the deeper plaza Figure 3.3.1's illustrative (non-dimensioned) rendering suggested -- treat the diagram's own depth for this specific feature as unreliable rather than assume more real room exists than the confirmed street position allows. EXTENDED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: since PKN grew, shrink it on the north side to give this plaza more depth): south edge (matching PKN's own north edge) moved south by 10m to match PKN's own north-edge adjustment -- see that file. Traced via programmatic pixel-color detection (isolating Figure 6.4.2's 'Public Open Space' fill color, RGB [194,218,106], with morphological closing to bridge small text/icon gaps, then an OpenCV contour extraction simplified to ~35 vertices) rather than hand-clicking, since this is a long, irregularly-shaped (and intentionally jagged/riprap-shore-like, per the diagram's own hatching) strip. Converted via this site's validated 6-point affine transform. Clipped against Parcels E1, E4, E3, and H2's own already-committed geometries via shapely difference() (the raw pixel trace overlapped each by a small amount, and building parcels take priority over this open-space trace) -- this produced a MultiPolygon with one large piece (~3.0 acres) and a smaller ~0.23-acre piece separated by H2. properties.project_name: Irish Hill Playground and Irish Hill Corner Plaza -- combined, approximate
properties.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155); named per Figure 3.4.1 - Overview of Public Spaces (p.52), zones 7 and 8.
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-17 in response to a user-caught gap: this project's whole open-space network for Pier 70 (Figure 3.4.1, p.52) lists 8 named zones, but only 6 had been traced -- Irish Hill Playground (zone 8, ~2.0 acres per the D4D text, 'an open space adjacent to the existing remnant of Irish Hill') and Irish Hill Corner Plaza (zone 7, no acreage given) were missing entirely. FIRST PASS: traced the green 'Public Open Space' fill (RGB [194,218,106]) directly from Figure 6.4.2's pixels, then clipped it against PKS/HDY3/C1/C2/HDY1-2's own committed geometries -- this ceded roughly 45% of the raw trace back to those neighbors and left an underestimate (~0.68 acres) that didn't visually touch several of the surrounding parcels. SECOND PASS same day: switched to the real, street-polygonized block (src/block_fit.py) bounded by Illinois St and 22nd St, unioned with PKS/HDY3/C1/C2/HDY1-2's own geometries, minus those same 5 parcels -- fixed the touching problem for PKS/HDY3/HDY1-2 but the user caught two remaining defects: it still had small (2.5m and 9.8m) gaps against C1 and C2 (the real street-block polygon's own edges don't line up exactly with C1/C2's independently-traced boundaries), and it incorrectly extended ~13m south of HDY1/2's own south edge (the real block reaches all the way to 22nd St's actual curb, which is slightly further south than HDY1/2's own, separately-traced south edge -- creating a sliver of 'phantom' park space south of a parcel that the diagram shows going straight to 22nd St). THIRD PASS: re-included the original diagram-traced raw contour (see first pass) in the union alongside the real block and the 5 parcels -- since that raw trace independently overlapped C1 by 1,142 sq m and C2 by 74 sq m, unioning it in extends the combined shape properly into contact with both (0m gap, confirmed) without the crude 'buffer everything outward' approach tried and rejected first (which fixed the C1/C2 gap but ballooned the total area to 3.3+ acres by reaching past C1/C2 in directions that had nothing to do with Irish Hill). Then explicitly clipped the whole result to never extend south of HDY1/2's own southernmost latitude, fixing the second defect directly rather than hoping the union wouldn't overreach. Also dropped one degenerate near-zero-area sliver piece (9e-6 sq m) left over from the boolean operations. Resulting area ~7,831 sq m (~1.94 acres). FOURTH PASS 2026-09-17 (streets/block-alignment review): PKS and HDY3 were both re-traced this same pass after a confirmed pixel-resolution bug moved them (see those files' digitization_method) -- HDY3 shifted to stay attached, but PKS moved further away, reopening a ~23m gap between this feature and PKS. The real, street-polygonized block (from the third pass) fell just 2.6m short of the newly-corrected PKS on its own -- a small, plausible real gap between the block-polygonization tool's edge and PKS's own diagram-traced edge, not the ~23m the raw union produced -- so the block polygon (only, not the parcels) was buffered outward by 6m before unioning, closing most of it; a residual 1.26m gap remains against PKS specifically, accepted as within this project's already-documented 5-15m trace precision rather than chased further with more buffering (which was tried at 15m earlier in this file's history and caused an unrelated overreach). Re-verified 0m distance / 0 overlap against HDY3, C1, C2, and HDY1/2, and 0 overlap with PKN and the 20th Street Plaza. Dropped a new degenerate sliver piece (~12 sq m) from this pass's boolean ops. Resulting area ~10,338 sq m (~2.55 acres) -- larger than the D4D's ~2.0-acre citation, mostly from the corrected PKS/HDY3 positions genuinely opening up more real space here than the earlier (buggy, too-far-south) PKS/HDY3 traces implied; not re-shrunk to hit the citation, since the citation was never used as a target, only a plausibility check. FIFTH PASS 2026-09-17 (REPLACED, user-flagged 'Irish Hill Playground seems misplaced'): the block_fit/union approach above was abandoned entirely. Looking at the actual diagram again, this green area is not just 'whatever real block Irish Hill roughly sits near' -- Figure 6.4.2 draws its exact boundary directly, including the hill's own contour-line hatching. Re-traced it the same way Waterfront Open Space was traced: isolated the 'Public Open Space' fill color (RGB [194,218,106]) in a crop covering the PKS/HDY3/C1/C2/HDY1-2 area, morphological close+open to bridge hatching/text gaps, OpenCV contour extraction (simplified to 15 vertices), converted via the validated 6-point affine transform. This raw trace overlapped HDY3/HDY1-2/C1/C2 by small amounts (each block's own black border stroke sits a couple pixels inside where the flat green fill visually ends), so it was clipped via shapely difference() against all four of those committed geometries -- same pattern as Waterfront Open Space's own clip against E1/E4/E3/H2. While investigating the C1 overlap specifically, found C1 itself carried the same 2376x1836-vs-2200x1700 resolution-mismatch bug already fixed on PKN/PKS/HDY3 (see pier70_c1.geojson's digitization_method) -- its true south edge is ~26m further north than previously recorded, which had been silently eating into this exact area. Fixed C1 first, then re-ran this clip. Result: 0m gap/overlap against HDY3, HDY1/2, and C2; 0.9m gap against the corrected C1 (within normal trace precision); the ~23m distance to PKS is NOT a gap to close -- the diagram shows PKS separated from this open space by the full width of HDY3, they were never meant to touch. This new trace does NOT surround HDY1/2 (no interior hole) -- the diagram simply doesn't show Irish Hill wrapping around it; the previous approach's 'surrounds on 3 sides' shape was an artifact of the block-fit/union method, not something Figure 6.4.2 actually draws. Area ~4,862 sq m (~1.20 acres), smaller than the D4D's ~2.0-acre citation -- as with the citation-vs-trace gaps already documented elsewhere in this project (e.g. Mission Rock Square), the citation is treated as a plausibility check, not a target; matching what the diagram itself draws, and touching real neighboring parcels correctly, takes priority. RE-CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (same day): C1 itself was found to be significantly mispositioned (overlapping the real 21st St by over 100m of its length -- see pier70_c1.geojson) and was moved south by ~28-31m to ground-truth against the real street. Re-ran this file's own clip against C1's corrected position; area dropped further to ~3,249 sq m (~0.80 acres). Confirmed 0m gap/overlap against HDY3, HDY1/2, C1, and C2. EXEMPTED FROM STREET CLIPPING 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: shape looked disproportionate/weird, 'as if leaving room for an expansion of Michigan street south which is nowhere in drawing'): exactly right -- Michigan St's real centerline (CNN 8999000) runs through this feature's own interior (same segment found splitting HDY1/2 into two pieces, see that file's digitization_method), and join_approximate.py's auto-clip was silently cutting this feature into a MultiPolygon around it (raw 3,249 sq m -> processed 2,782 sq m, a real but not obviously 'major' percentage that still produced a visibly wrong disconnected shape). Figure 6.4.2 draws this as one continuous green space with no street through it. Exempted from street clipping for the same reason as HDY1/2: this ambiguous, likely-informal site track (not a real curbed street at this latitude) shouldn't carve up a planned open space the diagram shows as whole. RE-TRACED 2026-09-17 (same day, user-flagged: 'the diagonal between HDY buildings seems disproportionate compared to HDY3'): correct -- overlaying the raw color-mask trace directly on page171.png showed a spurious deep V-shaped spike cutting into the middle of the green area, with no corresponding line or color break in the diagram at all (the green fill is fully continuous there). Root cause: a small tree/planting icon drawn within the green space broke the color mask into two blobs that a too-small morphological closing kernel (13px) bridged incorrectly, inventing a notch neither the diagram nor any real feature shows. Re-extracted with a larger closing kernel (25px, still small relative to the icon-to-real-boundary distance) to bridge the icon gap correctly; the resulting shape follows HDY3's own diagonal edge much more closely, with only a small, shallow, plausible dent remaining (matching a slightly darker hatching band visible in the diagram alongside HDY3's slope, not a hard error). Re-clipped against HDY3/HDY1-2/C1/C2; final area ~3,230 sq m (~0.80 acres, effectively unchanged from before -- this was a shape-accuracy fix, not a size fix). CHECKED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: 'should fill the space touching HYD3, HYD1/2, C1/C2, and 21st street'): re-verified this feature's touching relationships directly -- confirmed 0m gap/overlap against C1, C2, and HDY3, and a 3.7m gap against HDY1/2 and PKS (both within this project's already-documented 5-15m trace precision, not a real gap to close). The 'and 21st street' part does not hold as a literal requirement: this feature does not (and per the diagram should not) touch 21st St directly -- Parcel C1 (west portion) and Parcel K South (PKS, further west) occupy the FULL frontage between this open space and 21st St along this feature's entire north edge, confirmed by checking that C1's own north edge (ground-truthed against the real 21st St curb line) sits ~26-38m further north than this feature's own northernmost point, with no gap in that C1/PKS wall for this feature to reach through. This matches Figure 6.4.2, which draws Irish Hill Playground one row south of the C1/PKS/21st-St row, not fronting the street itself. RE-TRACED 2026-09-17 (same day, after PKN/PKS/C1/HDY3 were restored to their pure diagram positions -- see those files -- following confirmation that the '21st St ground-truth shift' premise was wrong, a paper-street issue, not a planned relocation): re-did this feature's raw color trace with a taller crop (extending north to y=740 instead of stopping at y=850-890) to check whether the green 'Public Open Space' fill extends further north than previously captured. It does: the fill runs continuously from y=775 (the same row as PKS/C1's restored, true north edge -- i.e. immediately south of '21ST ST (NEW)' itself) down through this site's full extent, confirmed by direct pixel scans at x=560/590/620 (the gap between PKS/HDY3's east edge and C1's west edge) showing the green fill starting at y=775-776 with no other color in between. This matches the user's own read of the diagram: this open space fills the space between PKS, C1, and 21st St. Extracted via the same method as before (isolate RGB [194,218,106], 25px morphological close+open, OpenCV contour), producing a 12-vertex main contour plus a separate ~158 sq m piece near Illinois St/HDY3's SW corner (the Irish Hill Corner Plaza zone). Clipped via shapely difference() against the restored PKS/HDY3/C1 and the separately-corrected C2 (see that file), plus HDY1/2 (unchanged). Result is a MultiPolygon: main piece ~6,299 sq m, corner piece ~158 sq m, total ~6,458 sq m (~1.60 acres). Confirmed within 1-1.6m (normal trace precision) of PKS, HDY3, C1, and C2, and 0.06m of HDY1/2. RE-CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (same day, after C1 was independently clipped against the real Building 113-116 footprint -- see that file -- shrinking it slightly from its pure-diagram size): re-ran this feature's own clip against C1's updated shape. Total area now ~6,458 sq m (effectively unchanged, C1's own change was on its north side, away from this shared boundary). RE-CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (same day, after PKN/PKS/C1/C2/HDY3/HDY1-2 were all repositioned against the corrected, real-anchored '21st St (NEW)' line and HDY3/HDY1-2 were both extended to the real 22nd St curb -- see those files): re-ran this feature's own raw diagram color-trace against all six updated neighbor positions. Total area drops from ~6,458 to ~4,258 sq m (main piece ~4,138 + corner piece ~120), mostly because HDY1/2's own growth (extending to the real 22nd St curb) now consumes much of what was previously open space south of HDY3. Confirmed touching (0-3.5m gaps, within normal trace precision) against HDY3, PKS, C1, C2, and HDY1/2. RE-CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (same pass, found via check_geometry_quality.py): also overlapped the repositioned (grown-south) PKN by 72 sq m along this feature's own north edge -- clipped that too. Final area ~4,186 sq m total (main ~4,066 + corner ~120). RE-CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (same pass as HDY3/HDY1-2/C2/PKN adjustments above): found this feature's own north edge crossed to the NORTH side of the '21st St (NEW)' reference line (data/manual/pier70_21st_street.geojson) by up to ~20m -- the raw diagram trace's own northern extent (unchanged since it was first color-extracted) was never re-clipped after PKS/C1 moved south in the prior round, since it had stopped overlapping them entirely. Added an explicit clip against a half-plane north of the '21st St (NEW)' line, plus re-clipped against the now-touching HDY3/HDY1-2 and the grown PKN. Area now ~3,673 sq m (main ~3,552 + corner ~120). RE-CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (same pass as HDY3/HDY1-2's redesign): with a real gap restored between HDY3 and HDY1/2 (see those files), this feature now fills that corridor down toward 22nd St, reconnecting into a single polygon (the separate ~120 sq m 'corner plaza' sliver from the prior round merges into the main body through this corridor). Area now ~2,615 sq m. Confirmed 0-5m gaps (normal trace precision) against all six neighbors. RE-CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (same day, after HDY3 and HDY1/2 were rebuilt a second time from the user's own hand-drawn sketch -- see those files' digitization_method): re-ran this feature's own clip against both blocks' new shapes. HDY3 now reaches further into this corridor than the previous round (322 sq m new overlap), HDY1/2 pulled back and no longer overlaps this feature at all (0 sq m, was already 0). Area now ~2,293 sq m, still a single Polygon (no fragmentation) and still 0m gap/overlap against C1, C2, PKS, and PKN. REBUILT 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: 'playground should fill the spaces between buildings as shown in drawing'): abandoned the raw-diagram-color-trace-plus-clip approach entirely (it had been producing a string of small, repeatedly-drifting gaps against one neighbor or another every time any neighbor moved, since the trace's own boundary was never actually defined IN TERMS OF those neighbors' edges). Rebuilt this feature directly as the walk around its neighbors' own already-committed boundaries, so it touches all of them by construction rather than by incidental proximity: HDY3's own NE corner (shared with PKS) -> C1's own SW and SE corners (its south edge) -> C2's own NE and NW corners (its north and west edges) -> HDY1/2's own NE corner (v1) and its newly-recomputed north corner (v0, see that file) -> HDY3's own corridor point -> close. Every edge of this polygon except one (the short HDY3_NE-to-C1_SW gap-filler, ~7m, since those two blocks don't quite touch) is now an EXACT shared boundary (0m gap by construction, not by measurement) with a real neighboring parcel. Area drops from ~2,293 to ~1,888 sq m, mostly because HDY1/2's own north corner moved east/north (see that file's own parallel-edge fix), shrinking the gap it leaves for this feature to fill. REBUILT AGAIN 2026-09-17 (same day, user-flagged with a hand-drawn overlay on the rendered map: 'playground should fill the spaces between buildings as shown in drawing... where I see the color missing'): the rebuild above only walked the 'upper gap' (C1/C2 vs the HDY3/HDY1-2 row) and left three real, satellite-visible open areas uncovered, all confirmed against the user's own marked-up screenshot (digitized via the same ORB-feature-matching + marker-calibration pipeline used for HDY3/HDY1-2's own hand sketch): (1) the HDY3-to-HDY1/2 CORRIDOR itself, from the shared top corner down to near 22nd St, was never actually added to this feature after being carved out as a gap between those two blocks -- added it back as the quadrilateral bounded by HDY3's own corridor edge (D to its 22nd-St/SW corner) and HDY1/2's own corridor edge (v0 to v3), which are parallel by construction (see those files). (2) A real, ~15-18m gap between HDY1/2's own east edge (v1-v2) and C2's own west edge (v0-v1/SW) -- the two blocks' side-by-side edges never actually touch -- confirmed geometrically (not just from the user's sketch) by comparing their longitudes directly. Added as the strip between them. (3) A smaller gap on the WEST side of C1 (between C1's own west edge and PKS's own east edge/the HDY3-PKS shared corner), which the user's sketch marked as a distinct notch reaching further north than this feature's previous extent -- taken directly from the user's own traced coordinates (no clean existing-polygon edges define this one), then clipped via shapely difference() against C1 and PKS since the raw traced notch initially overlapped both by a modest amount. All three additions unioned into one shape (still a single simple Polygon, not a MultiPolygon) and simplified to drop redundant near-duplicate vertices from the boolean ops. Re-verified: 0 overlap with HDY1/2, C1, C2, and PKS; a negligible ~1 sq m residual against HDY3 (rounding from the simplify step, not a real encroachment). Area grows from ~1,888 to ~4,236 sq m. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (same day, user-flagged again: 'you left out part of the space between PKS and C1'): root cause of the shortfall -- the notch above was clipped against C1's RAW, pre-street-clip geometry (data/manual/pier70_c1.geojson), which is NOT what actually renders on the map. C1 itself loses ~15m off its own west edge to a real-street clip in join_approximate.py (documented in that file's own digitization_method as '11.7% of this block's area... in the buffered real-street layer'), so the ACTUAL rendered C1 sits well east of its own raw west edge. Clipping this feature's notch against the raw file made it discard ~466 sq m that is genuinely open (uncolored) on the rendered map, not actually inside C1 at all -- confirmed by pixel-sampling the rendered PNG directly and by comparing against C1's own post-clip geometry in data/processed/approximate_projects.geojson (whose west edge sits at -122.38634 to -122.38637, ~15m east of the raw file's -122.38652). Re-clipped the notch against C1's PROCESSED shape instead (now a negligible ~3 sq m residual) while keeping the PKS clip (PKS isn't meaningfully street-clipped, so its raw and processed shapes already agree). Also swapped this feature's own touching point on C1's south edge from C1's raw SW corner to C1's actual post-clip corner, for the same reason. Re-verified 0 overlap against HDY1/2, C2, PKS, and C1's own processed shape. Area grows from ~4,236 to ~4,734 sq m -- this whole increase is the space that was wrongly ceded to C1's raw (non-rendered) footprint. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the earlier entry above saying Figure 6.4.2 draws Irish Hill Playground one row south of the C1/PKS/21st-St row, not fronting the street, was a misreading: on the rendered figure the green fill reaches 21st St between PKS and C1, as a later entry and the accuracy_caveat recognise. The earlier entry is kept as history. Nothing in the geometry was changed. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- traced directly from Figure 6.4.2's own 'Public Open Space' fill color (programmatic color-region contour extraction), then clipped against PKS/HDY3/C1/C2/HDY1-2's own committed geometries. Now extends north to touch '21ST ST (NEW)' directly in the gap between PKS and C1, matching the diagram's own drawn fill. The geometry is now a single Polygon: an earlier trace produced a separate small piece near Illinois St (the Irish Hill Corner Plaza zone), but it reconnects to the main body through the corridor between HDY3 and HDY1/2 (see digitization_method), and on the rendered Figure 6.4.2 the green band between HDY3 and HDY1/2 runs continuously to the Illinois/22nd corner.'; notes: 'Newly added 2026-09-17 as part of closing a gap the user pointed out: not all of Figure 3.4.1's 8 named open-space zones had been traced onto the map. Geometry redone multiple times the same day -- see digitization_method for the full history, including a full replacement after a user flagged this shape as looking misplaced.'. properties.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no Assessor lot of its own identified. Port Item 9B (2017) lists Irish Hill Park among 'Port improvements outside of the 28-Acre Site' and as a 'Port or Hoedown Yard Vertical Developer obligation, at Port's discretion', so it is not within Brookfield's 28-acre site; the earlier statement that it is is withdrawn. Assessor lots under it were checked on 2026-10-11: it lies on part of lot 4113001 (read by Pier & Point as part of the playground) and on parts of the Hoedown Yard lots 4110008A and 4120002 (see the accuracy note).
properties.regulatory_context: Part of the Pier 70 D4D's Open Space Network (Section 3.4): Irish Hill Playground (Section 3.12, ~2.0 acres), described as an open space adjacent to the existing remnant of Irish Hill (Section 3.2) -- an approximately 35-foot tall serpentine outcropping, today approximately seven percent of what the hill once was (D4D Section 3.2); the National Register nomination says Building 12 (1941) was built on newly leveled ground where most of Irish Hill once stood. The D4D does not say when or how the rest was removed. Irish Hill Corner Plaza (Section 3.11) is a separate, smaller named zone at the southwest corner of this same open area, near the Illinois St/22nd St corner.
